summary: The five Egyptian studies build Ke as Damodaran's "beta approach": rf* = local 10y (22.31–23.00%) minus Egypt's default spread (6.37% rating / 3.40–3.41% CDS), plus beta x total ERP (13.94% rating = 4.23% mature + 9.71% CRP; 9.41% CDS). Country risk is charged once net, but the charge is beta-scaled: on TMGH (beta 1.472) the CRP added is 14.29pp against 6.37pp stripped, so the net country charge over the raw bond yield is +7.9pp, versus +2.5pp on AMOC — that scaling is a house choice, not a Damodaran requirement (his lambda approach adds CRP unscaled, giving TMGH 32.6% instead of 37.15%). Nothing in the pipeline tests the LEVEL of the cost of capital against anything: wacc_builder emits warnings no study asserts on, assert_beta_provenance and check_study_provenance test the beta record's SHAPE, the Kd-integrity three-assert gate written into the protocol (§5) exists in no code (ARCC shipped with kd_gate.bound_met=false), the fundamental walk-forward scores drivers only, the R-GAP-01 review's DISCOUNT RATE heading asks "cash charged once", and the only place fair value ever meets price (value_gap_backtest, IC -0.14 at n=32) is a diagnostic with INSUFFICIENT-POWER. The measured pessimism is real but is NOT primarily the Ke formula: the DCF lens at house rates sits at -2.4% (ARCC), -2.2% (PHDC) and +7.4% (AMOC) of price; those three names' published gaps come from non-DCF lenses that capitalise earnings at 27–31% nominal with zero growth (PHDC NEP 5.17 at Ke 31.26%, g=0). The two biggest discount-rate defects are rule violations, not method questions: PHDC and TMGH were rebuilt 30-Aug/1-Sep-2026 on a FLAT spot WACC for every year and the terminal (PHDC 26.25% for 5y + TV at g=12%, TMGH 35.79% across 10 explicit years, a 14-year residual annuity and a recurring perpetuity), which the protocol's own r2 sliding-schedule rule (Standing_Research_Protocol.md lines 300–348, "governs every new Egyptian study") forbids; applying the AMOC-pattern norm-built terminal (rf_T 12.5%, ERP_T 7%, Kd_T 15%) with a 5-year glide moves TMGH's capacity case from 53.05 to 86.03 (-12% vs spot instead of -46%) and PHDC's DCF from 14.86 to 26.52 (central 16.19, +6.5% vs spot) at a coherent g=7%. Real Ke at 15% inflation is 10.8% (AMOC) to 19.3% (TMGH); every house Ke exceeds the realised EGX30 15y nominal CAGR of 17.0% (price-only) by 10.5–20.1pp and the 10y 21.9% by 5.6–15.2pp. The rating-vs-CDS basis choice is inconsistent across the five (AMOC/ARCC publish CDS, EGCH/PHDC/TMGH publish rating) with no rule and no out-of-sample evidence, worth 1.2–3.7pp of Ke, and the rating basis prices Egypt's default at 6.37% against a traded CDS of 3.41%. Betas are 5y weekly Dimson vs EGX30 with R² 0.26–0.33 and SE 0.16–0.18; Blume is computed as a "crosscheck" and never applied, Vasicek is absent; TMGH's beta CI90 [1.17, 1.78] alone spans Ke 32.9–41.4% and capacity value 47.3–60.8. EGCH's gap is not a discount-rate gap at all (implied flat rate 7.93%; even a flat 15% only reaches 1.18) and TMGH's residual gap after the glide is the sales fade and the minority.

summary: There is no house macro path: five Egyptian studies use five different year-1 inflation rates for the same fiscal year (PHDC 25.2% trailing, AMOC 14.5%, ARCC 11.5%, EGCH 10%, TMGH none stated), three different terminal inflations (AMOC 7%, ARCC/EGCH 5%, PHDC/TMGH ~14.6% implicit), two real-rate conventions (5.5% vs 3.5%), three sovereign yields (22.31/22.95/23.00%) and two terminal ERPs (7% vs 13.94% held forever); engine/market_profiles.py carries only rf_live=19.50% for EG and the Cost_of_Capital_Reference.md that CLAUDE.md points to does not exist. The single largest macro defect is not terminal growth but the terminal RATE: PHDC and TMGH discount their perpetuities at the crisis-era spot WACC (26.25% and 35.79%, rf* 16.63% + beta x 13.94% ERP) with no glide and no normalisation, which the full protocol's own KE/KD/WACC standing procedure (Standing_Research_Protocol.md ~lines 305-336: 'Sliding schedule - not flat', 'WACC_TERM < WACC_EXP is a hard ASSERT', 'Terminal ERP never held flat into perpetuity', applying to every Egyptian study next substantively updated) forbids, and no gate in research_protocol.py or scripts/ enforces; EGCH glides rf* but keeps the 13.94% ERP forever (terminal ke 23.0% nominal on 5% inflation = 17.2% real). Applying the house's own AMOC-style terminal (rf 12.5%, ERP 7%, kd 15%, g 7%) through the studies' own code moves PHDC's weighted central from 10.94 to 15.66 (above the 15.20 price) and TMGH's capacity case from 53.05 to 61.97 (70.39 with the fade restated in real terms). A second systemic defect is terminal reinvestment charged on NOMINAL growth against replacement-cost or constructed ROIC: ARCC reinvests 49.2% of terminal NOPAT to achieve zero real growth (rr = g/ROIC_repl, ROIC_repl 10.16% < WACC_term 16.46%), which is why its own grid says 'growth destroys value' (61.55 at g=3% vs 51.97 at g=7%); setting rr=0 for inflation-only growth on inflation-indexed capital lifts the DCF lens 57.60 to 83.24 and the central 54.10 to 66.92 (+13% vs the 59.00 price). Hidden real-terms declines remain in the shipped models: PHDC TG 12% (-2.3% real) and an NEP lens at zero nominal growth on a 31.26% Ke (-12.8% real forever), TMGH SALES_FADE 0.85 nominal (-25.9% real; found by its gap review at +23.46/share and NOT applied - model.py still carries 0.85), TMGH's 14-year level annuity valuing EGP 1,366bn of contracted book at EGP 1.1bn, ARCC's local and export cement price falling in real terms every year, EGCH's export urea path 530 to 440 USD/t (-5.9%/yr real USD) frozen into the perpetuity. Real-terms booms coexist in the same models (PHDC revenue CAGR 44% nominal 2026-30 from 25.2% price escalation on +15% deliveries; TMGH hospitality +20%/other +22% and a 20% deposit yield held flat for ten years), so the errors are not one-directional per model but the NET effect on value is pessimistic because the discount rate never normalises while the cash flows do. The walk-forward's mechanical inflation rule (trailing 3-year CPI, phdc_walkforward/bottom_up.py:102-108) was imported into the live PHDC study as the forward path, paired with a crisis discount rate that assumes no disinflation - fixing either leg alone moves value the wrong way (forward CPI 14.5% with flat WACC: DCF 14.86 to 10.44; with glide: 18.32), which is exactly why one coherent house path with a mechanical gate is needed rather than another review. L-048 and L-055 are registered at ALL scope but bind nothing: check_valuation_gap.py asserts heading text only, and both PHDC's and TMGH's gap reviews found macro defects that then shipped uncorrected. Macro coherence does not rescue EGCH (normalising its terminal ERP adds only ~0.9/share on a 13.98 price; its gap is the export price path and ANNA) or close AMOC/ARCC (already within 10%), but it is worth +40-45% on PHDC and +17-33% on TMGH before any cost-of-capital-level change.

layer: The four-lens blend and the non-DCF lenses (book value, normalised earnings power, relative multiples) across AMOC, ARCC, EGCH, PHDC, TMGH, against the ADNOCLS reference design
summary: On the three Egyptian names that actually blend four lenses, the DCF is NOT the source of the discount: PHDC's DCF is 14.86 vs 15.20 (-2.2%), AMOC's 9.77 vs 9.10 (+7.4%), ARCC's 57.60 vs 59.00 (-2.4%), and it is the three lenses blended around each DCF that pull the centrals to -28.0%, -5.0% and -8.3% (engine/phdc_study/gap_review_calcs.json lens_gap_contrib; engine/amoc_study/study_numbers.json lenses; engine/arcc_study/study_numbers.json lenses). The two lenses doing the damage are structurally biased down in a 15-25% inflation currency: normalised earnings power is capitalised at a NOMINAL Ke of 27-37% with zero nominal growth (PHDC: E/ke = 5.17/sh, an implied P/E of 3.2x against 12.25x paid by the market on the same FY26E EPS), which is a perpetuity whose real cash flow decays at the inflation rate, i.e. a run-off value, and the Fisher-consistent E/(Ke-pi) form is 1.7-2.2x larger at pi=15%; the book lens applies (ROE-g)/(Ke-g) with g=5-15% and Ke=31-37% to historical-cost book after a ~3x devaluation, producing justified P/B of 0.07x (EGCH), 0.075-0.28x (TMGH) and 1.0x raw (PHDC) against 1.7-4.8x the market pays on the five names. The lens weights (0.40-0.50 DCF / 0.20-0.25 relative / 0.20-0.22 normalised / 0.08-0.15 book) are typed 'study judgement' inputs in every study (adnocls compute.py:1649, amoc compute.py:533, arcc compute.py:769-773, phdc valuation_v2.py:151-155) with no out-of-sample test anywhere, which is the PROMOTION RULE violated by the house's own central number; and the fundamental walk-forward [R-FCAL-01] scores drivers only, never a lens value, the blend or the fair value, so the 'calibration' cannot by construction move fair value toward price. The same 'four lenses' are five different constructions across the five names (E/ke, E(1+g)/(ke-g), P/E 7.5x discounted 2.4y at Ke, P/E 7.0x on a doubly-haircut EBITDA, NOPATx10) and AMOC's relative lens is circular (own trailing multiple at 0% rerating = price less bridge deductions, so it can never sit above price). The ADNOCLS reference (UAE, pegged, Ke 9.43%, g 2%) transplants these constructions with no inflation adaptation, and its own blend came out +14.5% ABOVE price, so the design is not uniformly pessimistic; it becomes pessimistic exactly when Ke-pi is large. PHDC is built as a cash-conversion-ratio DCF plus P/E plus E/Ke plus raw book with no RNAV anywhere in engine/phdc_study/, despite the digest's LENS BY CLASS rule (RE developer -> SOTP/RNAV). On EGCH and TMGH the blend is not the story: TMGH publishes no blend (median of four cases 39.33, every case -39% to -77%) and EGCH's 'central' is the DCF-stopped case (3.34 -> 3.76 on main); there the discount rate (35.79% vs a price-implied 23.1%/19.4%) and the driver model dominate, and the gap reviews already found model defects taking TMGH's capacity case from 53.05 to 89.47 (-8.5%). The principal's premise that the projection method is systematically pessimistic is only half true on the repo's own record: PHDC's walk-forward found net profit OVER-forecast by +1.12 log in 97% of cells (optimistic), AMOC's found it UNDER-forecast by -1.02 log in 100% (pessimistic, worse than freezing) — the pessimism that survives to the fair value lives in the valuation layer (Ke, the two nominal-stasis lenses, the weights), not uniformly in the statements.

findings.claim: The normalised-earnings-power lens as built on PHDC (E / nominal Ke, zero nominal growth) is a run-off value, not an earnings-power value. Mathematically: a perpetuity of a FIXED nominal E discounted at nominal Ke = r_real + pi (+cross term) has real cash flow shrinking at pi forever; the no-real-growth EPV under Fisher is E/(Ke - pi) = E/r_real. Ratio Ke/(Ke-pi) at pi=15%: PHDC 1.92x, EGCH 1.92x, AMOC 2.20x, ARCC 2.13x, TMGH 1.68x; at pi=20%: 2.2-3.7x. what_the_repo_lacks: Any out-of-sample test of the lens weights or of the blend itself: no script, panel or walk-forward anywhere scores a lens value, a weighted central, or a fair value against subsequently realised prices or fundamentals; [R-FCAL-01] pre-registers drivers only (engine/Fundamental_Walkforward_Prompt.md lines 37-57) and [R-GAP-01] is a one-sided audit, not a calibration.

A per-class lens registry in engine/research_protocol.py: MODEL_STUDY carries only 'lens_pattern_references' (three company names) and a 16-section skeleton; the LENS BY CLASS rule lives in prose in the digest and is not asserted, which is how PHDC shipped as a cash-conversion DCF with no RNAV.

A Fisher-consistent specification for the normalised-earnings lens (E/(Ke-pi) or a real-terms E/r_real) and a rule that the lens's growth equals the inflation embedded in its discount rate — the same coherence [R-GAP-01] demands of the DCF terminal is not demanded of the two perpetuity lenses.

An inflation-adjusted or current-cost book lens (land, plant and hotels at market or replacement rather than historical cost after a ~3x devaluation), or an explicit rule that in a >10% inflation currency the book lens is a floor and is shown, not weighted.

A single definition of each non-DCF lens: five names carry five constructions of 'normalised earnings power' and four of 'relative multiples' (engine/phdc_study/valuation_v2.py, tmgh_study/lenses.py, amoc_study/compute.py, arcc_study/compute.py, egch_study/lenses.py).

A test of the house Ke against realised market returns (EGX30 10y 21.9%, 15y 17.0% vs Ke 27-37%), and a stated position on whether a perpetual Caa1 country premium (9.71 of the 13.94-point ERP) belongs in a terminal rate.

A rule on blend-vs-range: nothing in the protocol says whether the central is a weighted average or the DCF with cross-checks; ADNOCLS blends, TMGH refuses to, EGCH publishes a field, PHDC/AMOC/ARCC blend with different weights.
Own-history EV/EBITDA and P/E lenses computed from the committed panels for every name (TMGH has own_multiple_history; PHDC types '6x-14x roughly'; AMOC's is circular at 0% rerating).
open_questions: Should the central be the DCF (or the class lens — RNAV for developers) with the other lenses published as labelled cross-checks and a range, rather than a weighted average of four numbers whose weights have never survived any test? On the three blending names DCF-only alone moves the gap from -28.0/-5.0/-8.3% to -2.2/+7.4/-2.4%.

Is a lens-design walk-forward permitted under [R-LENS-01]? Price may GRADE a method but never enter it; grading each lens construction and each weight set against realised 1-3 year prices across the EG book would be a grade, not an input, and is the only way to earn weights under the PROMOTION RULE.

Which normalised-earnings specification is the house standard in a high-inflation currency: E/(Ke-pi) on trailing normalised E, a real-terms E/r_real, or a forward P/E anchored on the name's own history — and must the growth inside it equal the inflation inside its Ke, as [R-GAP-01] already requires of the DCF terminal?

Should the book lens be shown as a floor and carry zero weight in any currency with >10% inflation, or be rebuilt on current-cost/land-at-market book? On the five names the market pays 1.7-4.8x the book the house capitalises at 0.07-1.28x.

Does PHDC have to be rebuilt on an RNAV/SOTP lens per the LENS BY CLASS rule before any lens-blend conclusion is drawn on it, given TMGH (SOTP) and PHDC (cash-conversion DCF) are the same class on different lenses?

Is a perpetual nominal Ke of 27-37% (real 11-19%) — 6-15 points above the EGX30's own 10-year realised return — the right capitalisation rate for the perpetuity lenses, separately from whether it is right for the DCF? A 5-point Ke cut moves E/ke by +19% but E/(ke-pi) by +45% on PHDC.

ARCC: should the normalised base be the audited FY25 EBITDA (4,886mn) or the haircut 3,651mn, and should the relative multiple be the market's own 4.39x/6.14x or peers' 9.0x rather than a typed 4.5x/7.0x?

layer: FUNDAMENTAL CALIBRATION (statement walk-forward, [R-FCAL-01]) and its non-connection to the valuation layer
summary: The fundamental walk-forward measures ONLY the income-statement (and a few balance-sheet stock) drivers: log(projected/actual) per driver per horizon (h=1-5, or 1-3 on LIGHT), bias/MAE, block bootstrap over origins, skill vs two naive rules (freeze, 3y-CAGR trend), a macro-vs-company split and an era split. It never touches the discount rate, the terminal growth, the lens weights, the bridge or the fair value: across all five studies the only walk-forward number that enters any valuation arithmetic is ARCC's manufacturing-depreciation factor 1.0298 (engine/arcc_study/compute.py:480-487); PHDC/TMGH/AMOC/EGCH consume forward_ranges.json only as display bands for years 3-5 or as prose (phdc_study/valuation_v2.py:33-49, tmgh_study/statements.py:59-80, amoc_study/compute.py:2190-2221, egch compute.py:643-646). The principal's hypothesis is confirmed and is stronger than stated: even the income statement is barely recalibrated, because the corrections machinery has promoted exactly one number in ~170 cells (TMGH's four 'adopted' corrections carried 0.000 log into the forward path per forward_ranges.json, and the committed corrections_log.json is now EMPTY after commit 8fb64664 while the delivered study still claims four). Measured against the price, the walk-forward editions made the fair values WORSE on every name they touched (AMOC 5.95→5.53, ARCC 54.65→52.90, PHDC 15.89→10.94, TMGH 147.12→39.33, EGCH 3.64→3.79≈flat); every recovery (AMOC 5.53→8.64, ARCC 52.90→54.10, and the unapplied TMGH 53.05→89.47) came from the [R-GAP-01] manual audits, which found valuation-layer defects (cash double-charged, NEP at E/ke with zero nominal growth under 15% inflation, sales faded −26% real, minority on the wrong axis) that no statement calibration can see. The walk-forward record itself says the house method under-forecasts revenue on four of five names (AMOC −43%, ARCC −24%, EGCH −45%, TMGH new sales −58%) and loses to 'freeze last year's profit' at one year on four of five (skill vs freeze: PHDC −3.83, AMOC −1.13, EGCH −0.97 h1, TMGH −0.41 h1; ARCC +0.43), so the process is pessimistic on the statements AND the studies then build below the walk-forward's own centrals (TMGH FY2026 total revenue −23.5%, gross profit below the record's p10). The pessimism that matters most sits in the uncalibrated valuation layer: house Ke 27.5-37.2% (real 10.8-19.3% at 15% inflation) against an EGX30 that has delivered 17.0%/21.9% nominal over 15y/10y, with TMGH's own model implying 23.09% at the traded price; no gate in the repo grades a fair value against a later price, although [R-LENS-01] explicitly permits that measurement. The statistical design is honest about its own limits (5-13 origins, overlapping horizons, era flips on four of five names, a 0.5 correction strength that is a stated-not-derived free parameter) but that honesty means it cannot, by construction, answer the principal's question; a valuation-layer walk-forward is buildable now from what is on disk for 31 of 37 EG names (>=10 year-end closes) and 4 of the 5 calibrated names (>=12 statement years), with two data gaps (point-in-time EGP sovereign curve and ERP vintages; dividends for total return).

findings.claim: The discount rate is the largest untested lever and nothing in the repo grades it. House Ke (rating ERP) 27.45-37.15% on the five names = rf* 16.63-18.91% + beta(0.91-1.47) x ERP 13.94%; at 15% long-run inflation that is a REAL cost of equity of 10.8-19.3%. findings.claim: [R-LENS-01] permits grading a fair value against price and forbids only feeding price into the study. Exact text: 'A fair value never enters drift. The Fundamental_MC_Integration_Protocol.md §8 engine hook — value-gap IC into profile.ic — is permanently retired as a drift source … the value-gap IC may be measured forever as a diagnostic of the fair values themselves, and fv_overlay remains a downstream comparison surface. The repo already tried exactly this grade (Phase C value-gap backtest) and it was blocked on data, not principle: n=5, one-sided, and '30 of 31 EGX names carry exactly ONE fair value across the entire git history of assets/data.js … A value-gap panel needs vintages, and the archive is effectively one cross-section.' A valuation-layer walk-forward is the vintage generator that document said was missing. The one place the rule bites: a parameter chosen BECAUSE it minimises log(FV/P) makes the fundamental lens a consumer of price — so candidate constructions must be pre-registered from external principles and only SELECTED by the out-of-sample grade.

open_questions: Design of the VALUATION-LAYER walk-forward (proposed, for the synthesis): ORIGINS annual at each fiscal year-end from the first year with five years of statements (PHDC FY2015-FY2024 = 10; TMGH FY2015-FY2024 = 10; EGCH FY2012-FY2024 = 13; ARCC FY2018-FY2024 = 7; AMOC skipped or LIGHT), price taken at the first close after the FY statements were published (point-in-time). FROZEN AT ORIGIN: the statement-walk-forward's mechanical drivers as they stood at that origin (bottom_up.py already produces them), the house cost of capital rebuilt from a point-in-time sovereign yield + that year's Damodaran ERP/CRP vintage + the beta regressed on EGX30 data up to the origin (beta_regression.own_stock_beta with an end date), macro from the origin's WDI vintage (macro.json), terminal growth by the house rule as of that origin, lens weights as published, the bridge on the origin balance sheet. SCORE: e_h = log(FV_t / P_{t+h}) for h=1,2,3 (and vs total-return-adjusted price where dividends are held); bias, MAE, share negative, moving-block bootstrap over origins {2,3}, split-half by era (pre-/post-2016 float, pre-/post-2022 devaluations). DECOMPOSITION: re-run each origin with ONE lever at its realised or alternative value and attribute the change in bias — drivers at realised statements (isolates forecast error), Ke construction (house vs rf* + beta x mature ERP without CRP, vs implied-ERP), terminal g (house vs inflation-coherent), lens blend (DCF-only vs published weights), bridge (origin vs realised balance sheet); plus the implied-Ke series that equates FV to price at every origin (the TMGH 23.09% calculation, done 10-13 times). NAIVE BENCHMARKS: FV = P_t (log error = realised return), FV = own trailing 5y median P/E x current EPS, FV = own median P/B x BVPS; the house must beat FV=P_t at h=1 or it has not earned the precision. PROMOTION PATH for any construction change: candidates pre-registered from external principles (never fitted to the gap), scored LONO across names and split-half by era, adopted only where bias shrinks on held-out names AND eras without MAE worsening, with the price used as grader only — never as an input to a study's value ([R-LENS-01]).

Is the house discount rate the dominant lever? The evidence points that way (Ke real 10.8-19.3% vs index real ~2-6%; TMGH implied 23.09% vs 35.79%; PHDC DCF within 2.2% only after a 26.25% WACC) but it is untested; the valuation walk-forward's lever decomposition is the only honest way to say so.

Should the lens blend survive at all for asset-heavy/off-plan issuers? On PHDC the three accounting lenses produce 92% of the gap and the gap review calls them 'a floor rather than a value'; on ARCC the asset lens is the HIGHEST; no scoring exists for either choice.

Why did TMGH's corrections log empty in 8fb64664 without any gate noticing, and does the same scores.json reshape silently break corrections.py on any other name (PHDC/ARCC/EGCH write different shapes)? scripts/check_lessons_register.py anchors on run directories existing, not on the internal consistency of their files.

Does the [R-GAP-01] one-sidedness (fires only below price) now bias the book downward by construction — every audited name was pushed UP by its review (AMOC +56%, ARCC +2%, TMGH +69% unapplied), so a symmetric gate would presumably push over-optimistic names down; but with all five now below price the asymmetry is currently costless and untested.
AMOC has only five sourceable statement years: can a valuation-layer grade run on price alone (FV vintages need statements) or is AMOC a SKIP for the valuation test too?

Sourcing: which authoritative series gives point-in-time EGP 10y yields / T-bill rates back to 2011 (CBE, Ministry of Finance auctions, WDI FR.INR.*), and does Damodaran's ctryprem archive (annual since ~2000) satisfy SIGCM as a dated tier-C exogenous input for the historical ERP/CRP?

layer: EV-to-equity bridge, minority, cash, debt, dividends
summary: The five bridges are five different conventions, and the inconsistencies lean pessimistic by a wide margin, dominated by one item: TMGH deducts its minority at BOOK (EGP 75,652.8mn = 36.71/sh, 45.2% of equity) while the filed FY2025 profit split gives the minority 20.98%; re-pricing all four published cases at the filed profit share moves the median central from 39.33 to 60.09 (+52.8%, computed by re-running engine/tmgh_study/valuation.py bridge() with nci=0.2098). AMOC made the OPPOSITE choice on the same question — profit-share (EGP 405.4mn) instead of book (EGP 72.8mn), 5.6x book — so each study adopted whichever minority framing deducts more, which is not a method, it is a lean. PHDC deducts no minority at all (optimistic, about -0.44 on the central) but simultaneously leaves EGP 9,581.5mn of amortised-cost financial investments out of net cash, deducts EGP 9,380.7mn of land notes it itself says bear no interest as net debt while charging them at Kd 25.5% in the WACC weight, and stands on a balance sheet one quarter stale — net about +2.2/sh pessimistic on a 10.94 central. Cash is charged once in every study in the mechanical sense (no finance income in any FCFF, cash added at face), but the house has no settled theory of the weights: AMOC's delivered text says operations 'must be discounted at a HIGHER rate than the equity' and prints '27.45% — ABOVE the 27.45% cost of equity', while its code sets WACC = Ke (which is the gross convention the other four use); the study's own unlevering identity gives 32.34%, and applied to TMGH's net cash it would give about 46% — the prose, not the code, is the defect. AMOC's entire sensitivity and contested-choices grid is computed on a lighter bridge than the base (no provisions, no dividends payable, minority on EV only, raw ROIC terminal): the grid centre reads 10.71 while the published base reads 9.77, so the 'rating-basis 8.63' alternative is really 7.87 on the base bridge and the base is not in its own grid. Provisions (AMOC deducts EGP 996.9mn at face; TMGH 1,145.8 and PHDC 179.5 not deducted), dividends payable (AMOC deducts 258.3; TMGH ignores 376.6), FVTPL (TMGH omits 1,603.9), leases (in PHDC/TMGH/ARCC-weights, not in ARCC-bridge/AMOC) and the balance-sheet date of the weights versus the bridge (ARCC FY25 vs 30-Jun-2026) all differ across names with no rule. Of the twelve material inconsistencies counted, nine lean pessimistic and three optimistic; in per-share terms the pessimistic lean is roughly +21/sh on TMGH (53% of its central) and +2.2/sh net on PHDC (20%), against -0.4 to -0.6/sh optimistic items. No research_protocol assert exists for any of this; a bridge is attested nowhere and each study's builder invents its own.

what_the_repo_lacks: A research_protocol.assert_bridge(): no gate reads any study's bridge, share count, minority basis or balance-sheet classification; every bridge is hand-built per study with a different line set.

A house rule for the minority basis: the three framings (book, proportional, filed profit share) are never all computed, and the one adopted differs by study in the direction that deducts more.

A settled statement on cash in the weights: AMOC's delivered text asserts unlevering-for-cash while its code and the other four use gross weights; the digest's [R-GAP-01] text codifies the AMOC prose ('net cash => negative debt weight => equity weight above one => an operating rate above the cost of equity') as the defect without saying which convention is the standard.

A check that sensitivity and contested-choice grids return the base case at base inputs (AMOC's grid centre is 0.94/sh above its own base).

One ERP basis as primary: AMOC and ARCC publish on the CDS basis (rf* 18.91%/19.55%, ERP 9.41%), PHDC/TMGH/EGCH on the rating basis (rf* 16.63%, ERP 13.94%) — the same Egyptian sovereign priced two ways across five names (outside this layer, flagged because it changes what the bridge divides into).

summary: Across the five studies' gap reviews, QC gates, critique registers, self-audits and the lessons register I catalogued 65 recorded valuation-affecting defects (process/format defects excluded): 40 pushed fair value DOWN and 25 pushed it UP. Of the 40 DOWN defects, 19 sit in the statement layer (data/filing 7, driver 7, macro path 5), 19 in the valuation layer (cost of capital 7, terminal 4, lens 5, bridge 2, DCF mechanics 1) and 2 are false prose claims — so the pessimism is not concentrated in one layer, but the LARGEST items are valuation-layer or macro: the two hardcoded 18% WACCs replaced by 26.25%/35.79% (TMGH's −73.3% vs baseline is "essentially all of it the cost of capital", Driver Ledger), AMOC's FX path contradicting its own discount rate (+25% at UIP, missed by all four outside reviewers), TMGH's nominal sales fade (+44% on the capacity case), PHDC's zero-growth earnings-power lens (47% of its gap), and the 35.79%-vs-23.09% rate disagreement the TMGH review explicitly declines to call a defect. The same defect species recurred despite registration: macro incoherence (L-048) appears six times across four names (AMOC 06-08, 08-08, 01-09; EGCH; PHDC; TMGH), the terminal-real-decline (L-055) five times, unopened filings on the company's own archive three times, minority on the wrong basis three times, registered-but-unconsumed inputs (L-018) on three names after L-018 was written — and the register binds nothing by design ("no QC item consults it", PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS_01-09-2026.md). Detection is not self-auditing on the thing that matters: the gates (recalc, scrub, assert_sigcm, assert_beta_provenance, ground-up, table/figure discipline) caught zero of the six AMOC gap defects, AMOC's own E.1 reconciliation records that "nine of the ten largest priced findings came from outside", the net-cash double charge survived two editions because a reviewer's correct flag (GR7) was rejected with a "receipt" while another reviewer praised the construction (GT4/A-10), and every valuation-layer correction that moved a number was triggered by a human question, an outside critique, or the R-GAP-01 audit the human question created. The corrections found for PHDC (NEP at ke−g, latest balance sheet, NCI) and TMGH (SALES_FADE real, minority on profit share) are recorded but NOT implemented: valuation_v2.py line 146 still capitalises at ke with zero growth and model.py line 56 still carries SALES_FADE = 0.85. Finally, the digest's stated counterweight for its one-sided gate — "the fundamental walk-forward's own finding that this house leans optimistic" — is contradicted by the walk-forward record itself: revenue bias is negative on 4 of 5 names (AMOC −0.570, ARCC −0.278, EGCH −0.596, TMGH −0.090; PHDC +0.105) and bottom-line bias negative on 3 of 5; the optimistic finding rests on PHDC alone, and it is a recognition-clock specification error, not a lean.

layer: What the market price implies, and the reverse-DCF (five calibrated EGX names: AMOC, ARCC, EGCH, PHDC, TMGH)
summary: The five names do not share one error. Solving each study's own model for the market price gives implied discount rates that disperse from 7.9% (EGCH, engine/egch_study/study_numbers.json drivers.implied_wacc_base) through 19.4-23.1% (TMGH, lenses.implied_discount_rate) to 25.1% (ARCC DCF lens, interpolated from sensitivity.wacc_g), 26.05% (PHDC DCF lens, solved on valuation_v2.dcf) and above 30% on AMOC (its DCF lens 9.77 already sits 7.4% ABOVE the 9.10 price) — so no uniform cost-of-capital change can bring the book inside ±10%: the change that rescues TMGH (drop the 9.71% country premium, Ke=rf*+beta*4.23%) pushes AMOC to about +17% and PHDC to +24%. On three of the five the DCF lens is already within 8% of the price (AMOC 9.77 vs 9.10; ARCC 57.60 vs 59.00; PHDC 14.86 vs 15.20) and the published discount is manufactured by the cross-check lens blend: PHDC's -4.26 gap is -0.15 from the DCF and -4.11 from book value, own-history multiple and a normalised-earnings lens capitalised at a 31% nominal Ke with zero nominal growth (gap_review_calcs.json lens_gap_contrib). TMGH's gap is two specification defects the gap review already flagged as independent of price (a -15%/yr NOMINAL sales fade, i.e. -26% real, and the minority removed at its 45% book share against a 21% filed profit share): both corrected, the capacity case is 89.47 vs 97.80 (-8.5%) with no change to the 35.79% WACC, and the price then implies a 32.5% WACC — inside 3.3pp of the house rate. EGCH is the one genuine conclusion: no cell of its price x WACC grid (urea $380-540, WACC 17-24%) exceeds EGP 3.67/sh against 13.98, because the answer is the EGP 14.7bn unspent ANNA programme modelled at zero EBIT after depreciation, not the rate. The collapse of PHDC and TMGH fair values (15.89 -> 10.94; 147.12 -> 39.33) came from the v2 cost-of-capital step (WACC 18% -> 26.25%/35.79%: PHDC DCF at 18% is 48.50, TMGH capacity at 18% is 195.38), not from the fundamental walk-forward, whose adopted corrections were nil (AMOC 0/9 cells, PHDC 0, ARCC 1 of 12 = depreciation x1.0298, TMGH 4 of 15 with every revenue/profit driver refused) — the calibration measured that the method under-forecasts revenue on 4 of 5 names (AMOC -0.57, ARCC -0.28, EGCH -0.60, TMGH new sales -0.88 log) and applied nothing, while it over-forecasts profit on PHDC (+1.12 log, 3x, 97% of cells). The value-gap backtest is the only direct test of whether the house discount is information and it is powerless: n=32 one-month observations (15 origins, 11-Jun to 19-Jul-2026, 29 tickers, five calibrated names absent or carried at their OLD fair values), Spearman IC -0.140 (p=0.45), bootstrap PARITY, hit rate 56% (CI 39-72%), no 3-month outcome yet; sign-split shows house-'overvalued' names returned +6.7% excess and house-'undervalued' +5.7% in a month when 26 of 32 rose — noise, not evidence either way, and the clone in this session is shallow so it cannot be re-run. The pessimism is real and EG-specific at the book level (assets/data.js: EGX median fair/spot gap -15.1%, 26 of 37 below spot, 21 below -10%; ADX +1.3%, Tadawul +4.2%, DFM +22.7%), and two house-level inconsistencies are unrelated to any company: AMOC and ARCC (the two names near price) are priced on the CDS ERP basis (9.41%) while PHDC, TMGH and EGCH (the three far below) use the rating basis (13.94%); and PHDC/TMGH apply a flat peak-cycle 23% sovereign yield to every year including a 14-year annuity while AMOC/ARCC/EGCH glide to 16.5-19.8% terminals. Against the EGX30's own history (rolling 10-year price CAGR median 12.9%, p90 19.6%; rolling 5-year median 12.5%, p90 27.4%; 15-year 17.0%), a 31-37% cost of equity exceeds any return the index has delivered over any 10-year window, which is evidence independent of today's price that the rating-basis Ke is above the market's, but the cleaner names' implied Ke cluster (25.9-30.9%) says the defensible correction is a few points and a term structure, not the 8-14pp that would be needed to 'explain' TMGH or EGCH by rate alone.

summary: The fundamental calibration cannot fix the gap because the gap does not live in the statements: on three of the four Egyptian walk-forwards (AMOC, ARCC, TMGH) the method UNDER-forecasts the company's own filings (AMOC majority profit bias -64.1%, 0 of 9 cells over; ARCC PBT -45.7 log points; TMGH contracted sales ~58% low), the pre-registration rules then convert almost every bias into a 'watch flag' acted on by nobody (AMOC: zero corrections; ARCC: 1 of 12 adopted, x1.0298 on depreciation), and the valuation layer — discount rate, terminal, lens blend, minority — does the damage on top. The single largest mechanical cause on the two names the principal named is that PHDC and TMGH discount at a FLAT crisis-level WACC into perpetuity (PHDC 26.25% with g=12%, TMGH 35.79% with g=15%) in direct breach of the house's own 13-Jul r2 rule that retires flat WACC for Egypt, requires WACC_TERM < WACC_EXP as a hard assert, and whose own measurement says flat-vs-glide is worth +162% on an Egyptian DCF lens; both QC gates passed them without checking. Re-running PHDC's own DCF with the house glide (26.25% -> norm-built 16.26%, g=7% zero-real) gives 27.83/sh vs 14.86 published and a weighted central of 16.78 vs 15.20 spot (+10%); running TMGH's own model at its norm-built terminal rate (~22.6%) gives ~103/sh on the capacity case vs 97.80 spot, and the price-implied rate (23.09%) is literally the sovereign yield. The reference study (ADNOCLS) is not pessimistic in its own market — central AED 7.05 vs spot 6.16, +14.5% — and it normalises its terminal rf DOWN (4.48% -> 3.25%) in a pegged market; transplanting its 4-lens 40/25/20/15 blend, its 'hold full country ERP forever' terminal and its book/earnings-power lenses to a 23%-rf, 14%-ERP, 14-25%-inflation economy is where the pessimism is manufactured, and the house's own rules already say so (SRP line 493) without any gate enforcing them. The one external benchmark in the repo, EFG Hermes on ARCC (flat WACC 20.06%, g 2.5%, TP 69.75 Buy), sits almost exactly on the house's 5-year glide (cumulative DF 0.481 vs 0.471; bridge bar -0.16/sh), so on ARCC the disagreement is capex, terminal reinvestment and margin, not the rate — and the bridge judged zero of eight steps 'Testahil off mark', which is itself a symptom. The published bear/full envelope is a scenario spread, not a probability range: it is 20% wide on ARCC and 411% wide on EGCH, the price sits above 'full' on TMGH, and the central sits at the pessimistic end on four of five. Standard EM practice (USD Ke on a CDS-based CRP converted at the inflation wedge; real EGP at an 8-10% real Ke; sovereign-plus-premium) lands at 19-28% for Egyptian equity today with a forward decline, against the house's 27-37% held flat on PHDC/TMGH and a terminal cost of equity of 23% nominal on 5% inflation on EGCH.
